headline: ML-based feature selection nominates hub genes from multi-omics data in diverse diseases
label: Integrative Machine Learning Gene Prioritization
summary: Within individual studies, single-cell mapping, genetic causal inference and ML feature selection now jointly narrow candidate genes.
synthesis: The dominant thread is a gene-prioritization workflow in which transcriptomic or proteomic data are reduced to candidate hub genes by machine-learning feature selection. Across these items, WGCNA is combined with LASSO, SVM-RFE, random forest or Boruta to narrow candidate lists, as in six atopic dermatitis hub genes and CD36 in diabetic nephropathy. Several studies add genetic causal inference, using Mendelian randomization to link 65 immune-related genes to heart failure and to prioritize candidates in rheumatoid arthritis. Single-cell data then localize candidates to cell states, such as a CD36-associated macrophage state and fibroblast IGFBP5 in ulcerative colitis. A subset extends to molecular docking or dynamics, for example two docked lead compounds in ligamentum flavum hypertrophy and TLR2 and TNFSF10 in psoriasis and ischemic stroke. What is new here is the combination of genetic causal inference, single-cell mapping and ML prioritization within individual studies, rather than any one method.
